system_description.narrative_title: Fractured Global Order: AI, Finance, Energy and War
system_description.narrative_summary: The system is a tightly coupled, fast-moving global order where a tech-driven race (and its political capture) intersects rising macro-financial stress and regional wars. Major states, Big Tech, markets and energy flows are co-evolving: AI firms and U.S. politics push lax self-regulation even as regulators and safety warnings tighten, bond yields and central-bank policy transmit shocks across markets, and Middle East and Russia–Ukraine conflicts reshape energy supply and defence postures. These dynamics feed on one another, producing feedback loops—investment booms in AI and defence, policy interventions, market volatility, and renewed geopolitical rivalry—that make the system highly sensitive and hard to steer.
system_description.scope: Nation-states, alliances and militaries; major corporations (tech, energy, finance, defence); global financial markets and central banks; energy and commodity flows; regulatory institutions and legal processes; international mediators, NGOs and humanitarian actors; conflict zones and supply chains.
system_description.super_system: Planetary political-economic-security system (the globalized international order)

variables.name: Russia's war and hybrid campaign in Europe
variables.description: Russia is intensifying conventional, drone and hybrid attacks against Ukraine and targeting European infrastructure and companies, provoking NATO and EU defensive buildups and escalating East‑West tensions.

variables.name: U.S.–Iran stalemate and Middle East energy instability
variables.description: The United States and Iran (and their regional proxies) remain locked in a low‑intensity war and diplomatic deadlock that is disrupting Gulf oil flows, raising global fuel costs and forcing mediated talks and sanctions maneuvers.

variables.name: Global AI governance and Big Tech competition
variables.description: Leading tech firms, national regulators and international bodies are contesting safety, data access and market control as companies race to field powerful AI systems, reshaping industrial dominance, security rules and regulatory regimes.

variables.name: Global bond-market rout and monetary re‑pricing
variables.description: Surging Treasury and sovereign yields and persistent inflation expectations are re‑pricing risk worldwide, forcing tighter central‑bank policy, straining corporate financing and altering cross‑border capital flows.

variables.name: China's regional power projection and economic resilience
variables.description: China is combining military presence in neighboring states, industrial policy and targeted overseas investment while pushing back against external trade and tech curbs as it manages slower domestic growth and strategic competition.
